extracted.intended_audience: researchers, university grant administrators, and policymakers interested in historical NSF program/award listings
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and interpret program names, award types, and associated activity descriptions from an NSF (or similar) grants/awards listing (travel support, information systems, translations, education support, etc.). The page is a catalog of funded projects and program headings with brief activity descriptions and award amounts/durations.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPECIAL FOREIGN CURRENCY-TRAVEL SUPPORT
rubrics_metrics.description: Program heading listing travel awards (often in foreign currency) to support travel for U.S. scientists to attend conferences, present lectures, conduct research, or develop cooperative projects with foreign scientific institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries under this heading illustrate eligible activities: travel to attend international conferences and symposia, visits to foreign institutes to conduct research or negotiate cooperative projects, and presentation of lectures. Each award lists duration (months) and amount; some awards are noted explicitly as 'special foreign currency travel award (in Polish currency / Indian rupees / Soviet rubles, etc.)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: INTERNATIONAL COOPERATIVE SCIENTIFIC ACTIVITIES
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for international cooperative scientific work: visits, exchanges, collaborative research, workshops, and program organization with foreign partners and institutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include travel to discuss collaborative research programs, developmental visits for cooperative projects, exchanges to work at foreign laboratories, and support for international workshops/series. Awards are described with destination, purpose (e.g., 'to develop cooperative projects'), months, and dollar amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: SCIENCE INFORMATION SERVICES
rubrics_metrics.description: Overarching category for support of programs that create, improve, operate, or research scientific and technical information services and bibliographic resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections and example projects include development of thesauri for political sciences, bibliographic databases, operational tests of information systems, publication/distribution of proceedings, and contracts for computer-based handling of scientific information. Entries show institutional recipients, project titles, durations, and funding amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: SYSTEMS DEVELOPMENT AND IMPROVEMENT — INFORMATION SYSTEMS
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding for development, improvement, and operational testing of computer-based information systems and bibliographic data bases for scientific disciplines and research libraries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: contracts for computerized bibliographic databases, operational testing of national information systems, library systems development, university-centered information system projects, and development of retrieval/handling systems. Typical deliverables implied: thesauri, databases, operational tests, and system implementations.

rubrics_metrics.name: CHEMICAL INFORMATION
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts and projects specifically targeted at developing computer-based information handling systems and databases for chemistry and chemical engineering information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include multiple contracts for the development of computer-based information handling systems for chemical engineering, computer-managed databases for chemistry/chemical engineering, and production of expository information derived from Chemical Abstracts-type services.

rubrics_metrics.name: SCIENCE INFORMATION RESEARCH
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for research and studies into the foundations, organization, sharing, and impact of scientific and technical information systems and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative projects: logical foundations of information retrieval, analyses of potential benefits through sharing library resources, examinations of newly emerging scientific and technical information services, statistical studies of citation characteristics, and investigations of manipulation/specifications for large data bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOREIGN SCIENCE SERVICES AND PUBLICATIONS — TRANSLATIONS (DOMESTIC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for translation, publication, and domestic distribution of foreign scientific and technical journals and literature into English for use within the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: translation and distribution of Russian scientific journals, publication of translated monographs, and contracts to produce English-language versions of foreign scientific material. Awards list volumes, durations, and funding amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOREIGN SCIENCE SERVICES AND PUBLICATIONS — TRANSLATIONS (SPECIAL FOREIGN CURRENCY)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts and awards to support translation/processing of foreign scientific and technological information where payment or activity involves foreign currency, or to support translation efforts abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include named contractors and institutions receiving multi-year awards (often $100,000 or similar) to process foreign scientific/technical information into English; entries specify country/currency context and funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOREIGN SCIENCE SERVICES AND PUBLICATIONS — PROCESS IN ENGLISH FOREIGN SCIENTIFIC AND TECHNOLOGICAL INFORMATION
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects contracted to process foreign scientific and technological information into English (editing, translation, printing, binding, shipment) for dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contract recipients and amounts are listed; activities include translation, editing, printing, binding, and bulk shipment of foreign scientific literature, and establishing processing operations in-country.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPECIAL PROJECTS
rubrics_metrics.description: Miscellaneous support for institutional projects not fitted under other narrow program headings — e.g., expansion of university information centers, library system development, and publication projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: expansion of an information center, library systems development for a large research library, and multi-year publication or bibliographic projects. Awards indicate institution, project title, duration, and funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: SCIENCE EDUCATION SUPPORT — STUDENT DEVELOPMENT
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for student science training programs at various levels (precollege, college, summer schools), including programs to train and develop students in science and related disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries include institution-led 'student science training programs', 'student science training (pre-college)', summer schools, and mobile laboratory projects. Each listing shows program type (precollege/college), months (typically 10–12 months), and funding amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: SCIENCE EDUCATION SUPPORT — PRECOLLEGE LEVEL
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding targeted specifically at precollege science education and training programs intended to prepare secondary-school students for science studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: precollege student science training programs run by universities or colleges, regional conferences for elementary/secondary schools, and science mobile laboratory projects for youth and communities. Awards list program durations and budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: INFORMATION SYSTEMS — BIBLIOGRAPHIC AND DISCIPLINE-SPECIFIC DATA BASES
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for creation/operation of bibliographic services and discipline-specific databases (e.g., flora, taxonomy, geological reference files, biological abstracts, and other domain bibliographies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Flora North America program, Geological Reference File operational projects, bibliographic services in ichthyology/herpetology, ecological and taxonomic data bases, and conversion of index data into machine-readable form. Often multi-year and institutionally hosted.
